letters.desc: AEMA urges transmission owners and RTOs to disclose specific grid constraints and curtailment obligations during the study process so loads can make informed decisions about entering the FLFT.
quotes: To comply with Principle 7 of the ANOPR and for large loads to decide whether they can be curtailable, transmission owners and RTOs must provide transparency during the study process regarding the specific constraints that a large load would create and the frequency and amount of curtailment that would be necessary.

letters.desc: Transmission operators must transparently identify and disclose the specific constraints, hours, and system conditions driving upgrade needs. This transparency, as demonstrated by PG&E's Flex Connect model, allows customers to develop targeted solutions and accelerates interconnections.
quotes: Ensure a transparent interconnection process for large loads, where the transmission owners and regional system operators ("RTO/ISOs") provide customers with the specific constraints, system conditions, and/or the hours that are driving the need for new system upgrades and investment. The clear identification of system needs will allow customers to develop solutions to address those needs.

The wholesale markets have offered a place for customers to bring creative solutions to meet the system's needs cost-effectively. While this marketplace for innovation is available for many market services, a similar opportunity for transmission service does not exist for load customers because of the inflexible and opaque way in which load connection studies are conducted.

Pacific Gas & Electric's ("PG&E") "Flex Connect" Program offers the Commission a useful model for the transparency they should require of Transmission Owners. In constrained areas of PG&E's grid, PG&E identifies the hours and amount that customers need to curtail (or otherwise provide flexibility from on-site energy generation or storage) if they wish to defer upgrades and interconnect immediately.

letters.desc: GridCARE recommends that transmission providers publish hosting capacity maps or locational headroom indicators so large-load customers can identify the most feasible interconnection sites and reduce queue uncertainty.
quotes: the Commission could encourage or require transmission providers to publish transmission level hosting capacity maps or locational headroom indicators that give large load customers signals on where interconnection is most feasible.

letters.desc: iMasons asks that utilities be required to give developers early access to anticipated costs (state and FERC jurisdictional) and draft agreements, so developers can make informed decisions and speculative projects exit queues sooner.
quotes: interconnecting utilities should be required to provide large load developers with: 1) sufficient information regarding anticipated state-jurisdictional and FERC-jurisdictional costs that they will be expected to bear, including a clear understanding of how FERC-jurisdictional costs are expected to be reflected in retail rates; and 2) drafts of all relevant agreements that they will need to execute to interconnect their projects.

letters.desc: Utility operators must file documentation on data center interconnection terms, conditions of service, and pricing with state and federal agencies to enable ratepayer protection and market transparency.
quotes: Require utility operators to file documentation related to data centers with appropriate state and federal regulatory agencies that detail terms and conditions of service and associated prices to facilitate transparency and protect rate payers.
